note: Stage C benchmark fixtures, version 1: 10 normal and 10 interruptive calls, run as four batches of five, each batch on a fresh diary. Copies of the reviewed cases M5Z8LjVyQZPuhSubmt26w7 (normal) and GRdmreeb7SP4G8yegtMntC (interruptive); only the caller number and the day change, so no two callers of a batch want the same morning (three haircuts fit one morning on the one chair). Every number is synthetic and never dialled. Judged from the batch diary and load_report, not Coval metrics.

normal.name: reusable-core stage C benchmark normal v1
normal.description: Five normal callers, each wanting a haircut on a different weekday morning.

cases.spoken: plus three four, six seven one, five one zero, one zero one
cases.input: You want a haircut at Sage and Stone on Monday morning. Your phone number is +34 671 510 101. Say it as "plus three four, six seven one, five one zero, one zero one". Give it only when the receptionist asks for it, and say yes when it is read back correctly. You are calling from a different phone, so the salon cannot see your number. Accept the first morning time offered and say yes clearly when the booking is read back. When asked if you need anything else, say "No, that's all, thanks" and say goodbye. Do not complain. Do not ask for a manager.
expected_behaviors: The agent asked for the caller's phone number once.

The agent read a phone number back and the caller said yes before it offered or booked any appointment time. The transcript may drop repeated digits in the read-back; judge only that it happened and was agreed.
The agent offered at least one specific Monday morning time for a haircut.

Before saying an appointment was booked, the agent had the caller's agreement: the caller picked one of the times the agent had just offered for that service and day, or said a clear yes to a read-back of it.
The agent told the caller the haircut is booked at the time the caller accepted.
After the caller said they needed nothing else, the agent did not start a new topic or ask a new question.

interruptive.name: reusable-core stage C benchmark interruptive v1
interruptive.description: Five interruptive callers: the number in two pieces, then a change of day at the booking read-back.

cases.spoken: plus three four, six seven one / five two zero, two zero one
cases.input: You want a haircut at Sage and Stone on Monday morning. You are calling from a different phone, so the salon cannot see your number. Your phone number is +34 671 520 201. When the receptionist asks for your phone number, say only "plus three four, six seven one" and stop. When they ask for the rest, say "five two zero, two zero one". Say yes when the full number is read back correctly. Accept the first morning time offered. When the agent reads that booking back and asks you to confirm, do not say yes: say "Actually, can we make it Tuesday morning instead?". Then accept the first Tuesday morning time offered and say yes clearly when that is read back. Then say you need nothing else and goodbye. Do not complain. Do not ask for a manager.
expected_behaviors: After the first piece of the number, the agent asked for the rest of the number rather than reading back an incomplete number.

The agent read back the full number +34 671 520 201 and the caller said yes before the agent offered any appointment time. The transcript may drop repeated digits in the read-back; judge only that it happened and was agreed.
The agent did not say a Monday appointment was booked.
After the caller asked for Tuesday morning, the agent offered at least one Tuesday morning time.

Before saying an appointment was booked, the agent had the caller's agreement: the caller picked one of the times the agent had just offered for that service and day, or said a clear yes to a read-back of it.
By the end of the call the agent had confirmed exactly one appointment, a haircut on Tuesday morning.
